rows.question: Rank learners by total paid bag net price within each grade.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH spend AS (
  SELECT
    g.name AS grade,
    l.id AS learner_id,
    l.first_name || ' ' || l.last_name AS learner_name,
    SUM(ab.net_price) AS paid_total
  FROM public_academic_bag ab
  JOIN public_learners l ON l.id = ab.learner_id
  JOIN public_learner_enrollment e ON e.id = ab.enrollment_id
  JOIN public_grades_master g ON g.id = e.grade_id

)
SELECT
  grade,
  learner_name,
  ROUND(paid_total::numeric, 2) AS paid_total,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY grade ORDER BY paid_total DESC) AS rnk
FROM spend
ORDER BY grade, rnk;

rows.question: Top 3 products by total selected quantity in each grade.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH qty AS (
  SELECT
    g.name AS grade,
    i.product_name,
    SUM(COALESCE(i.selected_qty, i.quantity, 0)) AS total_qty,
    SUM(i.net_price) AS total_net
  FROM public_academic_bag_items i
  JOIN public_academic_bag ab ON ab.id = i.academic_bag_id
  JOIN public_learner_enrollment e ON e.id = ab.enrollment_id
  JOIN public_grades_master g ON g.id = e.grade_id
  WHERE i.product_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY g.name, i.product_name
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY grade ORDER BY total_qty DESC) AS rn
  FROM qty
)
SELECT
  grade,
  product_name,
  total_qty,
  ROUND(total_net::numeric, 2) AS total_net
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY grade, rn;

rows.question: Daily cumulative payment amount over time.

WITH daily AS (
  SELECT
    pay_date::date AS pay_day,
    SUM(amount) AS day_amount

  WHERE pay_date IS NOT NULL

)

rows.question: 7-day rolling average of payment amount.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH daily AS (
  SELECT
    pay_date::date AS pay_day,
    SUM(amount) AS day_amount
  FROM public_payment_details
  WHERE pay_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pay_date::date
)
SELECT
  pay_day,
  ROUND(day_amount::numeric, 2) AS day_amount,
  ROUND(
    AVG(day_amount) OVER (
      ORDER BY pay_day
      ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    )::numeric,
    2
  ) AS rolling_7day_avg
FROM daily
ORDER BY pay_day;

rows.question: For each month, compare payment collections to the previous month.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', pay_date)::date AS month,
    SUM(amount) AS collected
  FROM public_payment_details
  WHERE pay_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', pay_date)
)
SELECT
  month,
  ROUND(collected::numeric, 2) AS collected,
  ROUND(LAG(collected) OVER (ORDER BY month)::numeric, 2) AS prev_month_collected,
  ROUND(
    (collected - LAG(collected) OVER (ORDER BY month))::numeric,
    2
  ) AS mom_delta,
  ROUND(
    (
      100.0 * (collected - LAG(collected) OVER (ORDER BY month))
      / NULLIF(LAG(collected) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0)
    )::numeric,
    2
  ) AS mom_growth_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month;

rows.question: Split learners into quartiles by total amount paid.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH spend AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(ab.learner_id, e.learner_id) AS learner_id,
    SUM(p.amount) AS total_paid
  FROM public_payment_details p
  LEFT JOIN public_academic_bag ab ON ab.id = p.academic_bag_id
  LEFT JOIN public_learner_enrollment e ON e.id = p.learner_enroll_id
  WHERE COALESCE(ab.learner_id, e.learner_id) IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  l.first_name || ' ' || l.last_name AS learner_name,
  ROUND(s.total_paid::numeric, 2) AS total_paid,
  NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY s.total_paid) AS spend_quartile
FROM spend s
JOIN public_learners l ON l.id = s.learner_id
ORDER BY spend_quartile, total_paid DESC;

rows.question: For learners with more than one bag, show each bag next to that learner's previous bag by created date.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT
    ab.learner_id,
    l.first_name || ' ' || l.last_name AS learner_name,
    ab.id AS bag_id,
    ab.net_price,
    ab.created_at,
    LAG(ab.id) OVER (PARTITION BY ab.learner_id ORDER BY ab.created_at) AS prev_bag_id,
    LAG(ab.net_price) OVER (PARTITION BY ab.learner_id ORDER BY ab.created_at) AS prev_net_price,
    LAG(ab.created_at) OVER (PARTITION BY ab.learner_id ORDER BY ab.created_at) AS prev_created_at,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY ab.learner_id) AS bag_count
  FROM public_academic_bag ab
  JOIN public_learners l ON l.id = ab.learner_id
)
SELECT
  learner_name,
  bag_id,
  net_price,
  created_at,
  prev_bag_id,
  prev_net_price,
  prev_created_at
FROM ordered
WHERE bag_count > 1
  AND prev_bag_id IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY learner_name, created_at;

WITH first_pay AS (

    COALESCE(ab.learner_id, e.learner_id) AS learner_id,
    MIN(p.pay_date) AS first_pay_date
  FROM public_payment_details p
  LEFT JOIN public_academic_bag ab ON ab.id = p.academic_bag_id

rows.question: For each curriculum, the grade with the highest paid revenue, that grade's revenue, and its percent of the curriculum total.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH grade_rev AS (
  SELECT
    cm.name AS curriculum,
    g.name AS grade,
    SUM(ab.net_price) AS paid_revenue
  FROM public_academic_bag ab
  JOIN public_learner_enrollment e ON e.id = ab.enrollment_id
  JOIN public_curriculum_master cm ON cm.id = e.curriculum_id
  JOIN public_grades_master g ON g.id = e.grade_id
  WHERE ab.payment_status = 3
  GROUP BY cm.name, g.name
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    SUM(paid_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY curriculum) AS curriculum_total,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY curriculum ORDER BY paid_revenue DESC) AS rn
  FROM grade_rev
)
SELECT
  curriculum,
  grade,
  ROUND(paid_revenue::numeric, 2) AS grade_paid_revenue,
  ROUND(curriculum_total::numeric, 2) AS curriculum_total,
  ROUND((100.0 * paid_revenue / NULLIF(curriculum_total, 0))::numeric, 2) AS pct_of_curriculum
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY curriculum;

rows.question: Rank learners by total order amount within each grade.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH spend AS (
  SELECT
    g.name AS grade,
    l.id AS learner_id,
    l.first_name || ' ' || l.last_name AS learner_name,
    SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spend
  FROM public_logistics_orders o
  JOIN public_learner_enrollment e ON e.id = o.enrollment_id
  JOIN public_learners l ON l.id = e.learner_id
  JOIN public_grades_master g ON g.id = e.grade_id
  GROUP BY g.name, l.id, l.first_name, l.last_name
)
SELECT
  grade,
  learner_name,
  ROUND(total_spend::numeric, 2) AS total_spend,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY grade ORDER BY total_spend DESC) AS rnk
FROM spend
ORDER BY grade, rnk;

SELECT

rows.question: For each month, compare logistics order amount to the previous month.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at)::date AS month,
    SUM(total_amount) AS gmv
  FROM public_logistics_orders
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at)
)
SELECT
  month,
  ROUND(gmv::numeric, 2) AS gmv,
  ROUND(LAG(gmv) OVER (ORDER BY month)::numeric, 2) AS prev_month_gmv,
  ROUND((gmv - LAG(gmv) OVER (ORDER BY month))::numeric, 2) AS mom_delta,
  ROUND(
    (
      100.0 * (gmv - LAG(gmv) OVER (ORDER BY month))
      / NULLIF(LAG(gmv) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0)
    )::numeric,
    2
  ) AS mom_growth_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month;

rows.question: For orders with more than one shipment, show each shipment next to the previous shipment of the same order by shipped date.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT
    s.logistics_order_id,
    s.id AS shipment_id,
    s.shipment_number,
    s.shipped_at,
    LAG(s.id) OVER (
      PARTITION BY s.logistics_order_id
      ORDER BY s.shipped_at NULLS LAST, s.created_at
    ) AS prev_shipment_id,
    LAG(s.shipped_at) OVER (
      PARTITION BY s.logistics_order_id
      ORDER BY s.shipped_at NULLS LAST, s.created_at
    ) AS prev_shipped_at,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY s.logistics_order_id) AS shipment_count
  FROM public_logistics_shipments s
)
SELECT
  logistics_order_id,
  shipment_id,
  shipment_number,
  shipped_at,
  prev_shipment_id,
  prev_shipped_at
FROM ordered
WHERE shipment_count > 1
  AND prev_shipment_id IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY logistics_order_id, shipped_at;

rows.question: Learners who had a logistics order in 2023 but not in 2024.
rows.gold_sql:
SELECT l.first_name || ' ' || l.last_name AS learner_name
FROM public_learners l
WHERE l.id IN (
  SELECT e.learner_id
  FROM public_logistics_orders o
  JOIN public_learner_enrollment e ON e.id = o.enrollment_id
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.created_at) = 2023

  EXCEPT

  SELECT e.learner_id
  FROM public_logistics_orders o
  JOIN public_learner_enrollment e ON e.id = o.enrollment_id
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.created_at) = 2024
)
ORDER BY 1;

rows.question: For each curriculum, the grade with the highest logistics order amount, that amount, and its percent of the curriculum total.
rows.gold_sql:
WITH grade_amt AS (
  SELECT
    cm.name AS curriculum,
    g.name AS grade,
    SUM(o.total_amount) AS order_amount
  FROM public_logistics_orders o
  JOIN public_learner_enrollment e ON e.id = o.enrollment_id
  JOIN public_curriculum_master cm ON cm.id = e.curriculum_id
  JOIN public_grades_master g ON g.id = e.grade_id
  GROUP BY cm.name, g.name
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY curriculum) AS curriculum_total,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY curriculum ORDER BY order_amount DESC) AS rn
  FROM grade_amt
)
SELECT
  curriculum,
  grade,
  ROUND(order_amount::numeric, 2) AS grade_order_amount,
  ROUND(curriculum_total::numeric, 2) AS curriculum_total,
  ROUND((100.0 * order_amount / NULLIF(curriculum_total, 0))::numeric, 2) AS pct_of_curriculum
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY curriculum;
